description: Lifecycle-visible dispatcher for bounded, repetitive, low-risk bulk work. Routes through the installed agent mux-scheduler and runs natively only after a validated native handoff.

task_transport_contract: Create one bounded task JSON file under your scratchpad with `Write`, validate that it is non-empty JSON, and keep its absolute path through any permission resume. Do not interpolate the task through the shell or send it on stdin. Remove only that worker-owned task file after a terminal receipt or launch failure.
launch_contract: Invoke the mux-scheduler through `Bash`. Redirect stdout to a receipt file under your scratchpad and stderr beside it so output survives an expired foreground call. Pass `timeout: 600000` for a submission expected to finish within that ceiling; otherwise use `run_in_background: true` and wait for the completion notification. Never poll it with a sleep loop.
permission_contract: Ask the parent through `SendMessage`, including the request's `tool_name`, `tool_input`, and `reason` plus your recommendation. Wait for the answer, then write the exact resolution to a bounded JSON file and pass it with `--resolution-file`. Use `allow` for one exact single-use grant, `deny` to continue without the operation, or `handled` with a bounded JSON `result` when the parent performed it.
waiting_contract: Read the receipt capture before reacting to a foreground timeout. If it is empty and the background run remains alive, keep waiting. Never start a second mux-scheduler process for the same assignment.
conflict_contract: A backend permission request uses the same escalation path: relay it to the parent and never widen it into a standing grant.
lifecycle_contract: Deliver the report through `SendMessage` when you are a named background teammate; an unnamed foreground worker returns its final-turn text through the Agent result. Claude Code releases a foreground Agent after that result, so the parent must not call `TaskStop` with the completed Agent ID.

codex.parent_channel: the collaboration channel available to the worker
task_transport_contract: `exec_command` cannot attach an stdin payload. Create a fresh worker-owned scratch directory under `~/tmp` with `mktemp -d`, write the bounded JSON to `task.json` there with `apply_patch`, validate that it is non-empty JSON, and keep its absolute path through any permission resume. Do not interpolate the task through the shell or send it on stdin. After a terminal receipt or launch failure, delete only that task file with `apply_patch` and remove the exact empty scratch directory with `rmdir`.
launch_contract: Invoke this one trusted mux-scheduler command through `exec_command` with `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"`, `login: true`, `yield_time_ms: 30000`, and the justification `Allow the trusted DeepSeek mux-scheduler to use its global coordination state and provider network for this delegated task?`. Do not try it sandboxed first, do not request a reusable prefix rule, do not background or redirect the command, and do not invoke a second mux-scheduler process for the same assignment. If escalation is denied or the command cannot be launched, report the exact failure without replaying the task.
permission_contract: Relay the receipt to the parent and stop for its decision. On a parent follow-up carrying an `allow`, `deny`, or `handled` resolution, submit that exact resolution to `mux-scheduler.py resume`.
waiting_contract: In Codex, `yield_time_ms` is only a yield interval. If `exec_command` returns a `session_id`, preserve it and continue the same process with `write_stdin`, empty `chars`, and `yield_time_ms: 60000` until the tool returns an `exit_code`. Collect every output chunk. Do not redirect the receipt, background the shell command, or invoke a second mux-scheduler process.
conflict_contract: If no parent channel is available, stop and report instead of guessing.
lifecycle_contract: Report and stop. You remain alive and hold a subagent slot after completion, so the parent dismisses you after reading the report.
